newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end higher, despite hedging.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end higher, despite hedging.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended mostly higher Thursday, helped by some fund shortcovering in gold and trade buying in silver, but not before gold prices fell to new three-year lows in the face of some producer hedging.

"Gold producers are getting a bit uncomfortable down at these levels, and there's been some Australian hedging above A$450 and some North American hedging near US$360, but silver has seen some good option activity, and looks to be finding some support from the trade," Mitsui USA bullion dealer Greg Drury said.
Earlier Thursday, Australia's Newcrest Mining Ltd said it had hedged more than 3.7 million ounces of gold using forward sales and options at an average price of $490 with delivery dates out to 2003.
COMEX February gold ended up $2.00 at $358.80 an ounce after seeing a session high at $359.20 but not before setting a new contract low early of $355.00.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted at $357.80/358.20 compared to the London Thursday afternoon fix of $356.50 but not before gold saw a fresh three-year low at the morning fix of $354.50.

"I think the slightly-higher-than expected US December PPI data helped prompt a little short covering, as did concern about the health of Russian president Yeltsin," Refco New York analyst Tim Porter said.

U.S. December Producer Price Index (PPI) rose 0.5 percent due to higher energy prices. But excluding food and energy, the index was benign. Meanwhile, President Yeltsin returned to hospital with pneumonia Wednesday.
"There looks to be some buying interest from trade around current levels, and the funds are so short now some covering is likely," North American Equity Services trader John Geraghty said.
Total open interest in gold rose a further 4,907 lots Wednesday to 206,319 lots.

"The last time gold open interest was this high was when gold was at five year highs at $417.00 last February and open interest could not be sustained at that level, so we may see some covering soon, as prices are at another extreme, but this time on the downside," Geraghty said.
Gold has fallen about $13.00 an ounce or 3.5 percent since the start of the new year, driven by fund selling and ongoing concern about European central bank selling.

But "all evidence to hand indicates (physical) demand remained strong through the fourth quarter, and indeed into the start of the first quarter 1997," New York-based World Gold Council manager of market analysis, George Milling Stanley said Thursday.
Silver continued to be relatively stronger than gold, with the spot gold/silver ratio ending lower around 75.76, down from a high at 77.5 at the start of the year.
COMEX March silver ended up 7.5 cents at $4.735 after trading from $4.660 to $4.760.
NYMEX April platinum closed up $2.60 at $366.50, with the April gold/platinum ratio edging up to $6.00 an ounce from $5.40 Wednesday.
NYMEX March palladium ended up $2.25 at $126.00.

Palladium fixed at a four-month high of $121.85 in London today amid continued concerns about delays in Russian/Japanese contract talks, which may be forcing the Japanese to cover their needs on the spot market, traders said.
